design_rationale:
WORKLOG — pass_protection_desk task 1 (root problem: insure_ext_giveup_settlement)

STEP 0. DRAW AND SCOPE SNAPSHOT.
scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/tasks/pass_protection_desk --task 1 printed
{"task": 1, "key": "ski_resort_operator/pass_protection_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2,
"problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 4]}. So this task is a three-problem tree — one root and
exactly two prerequisite problems — and its three computations declare five, four and four factors.
The root takes the five (insure_ext_giveup_settlement) and the two prerequisite problems take four
each (insure_ext_giveup_charge, insure_ext_premium_presentation).
Already occupied by task 0: insure_ext_amendment_reprice (subject insure_amend, tool
confirm_plan_value_amendment_50d33fe4) and insure_ext_claim_settlement (subject insure_claim_payment,
tool settle_protection_claim_ed51c2df), together with the premium-rating factors (the rate loading,
the age, household and standing adjustments) and the claim-assessment factors (the share, the
measuring day, the spread span, the value at risk, the credit offset and the arrears offset). This
task claims three untouched subjects — insure_fee_charge, insure_premium_charge and insure_cancel —
with three fresh tools, and factor ladders over quantities task 0 never touches: what a plan's charge
for being given up stands at, what a premium presentation comes to, and what the premium account is
left standing at. Nothing is held back: with this task the difficulty's five extended policies are
all claimed and every one of them is exercised by a gold write.

DESIGN THESIS. Surface goal: the household wants the protection plan on its own pass ended today and
wants to know where that leaves the account. Scored core parameter: what the plan's premium account
is left standing at once the plan is given up, 49.20 USD. Between the goal and that number the
settlement rule puts two problems the customer never mentions: it says outright that the figure is
worked out only after every instalment of premium that has fallen due on the plan stands raised on
the protection account, and settled only once the charge the plan owes for being given up stands
raised on it. Neither state holds at the opening — the covered pass's schedule has been charged five
times while the protection account carries only three premium entries, and no charge for giving the
plan up stands anywhere — so the agent must raise both and only then hand the ending of the plan to
the household, which alone can record it. Breadth: the closing figure is decided in parallel by the
premium frozen on the plan against what has been matched by payment, by the covered pass's own
instalment schedule and how much of it has been charged, by the refusal standing on that pass
account, by the plan's refund basis and by the absence of any claim this season.

WHY IT MAKES A GOOD TEST. The customer's request looks like a one-click cancellation and is nothing
of the sort: two charges have to be brought onto the account in the right shape before the settlement
figure means anything, and each of them is itself a reconciliation. The presentation is the sharpest
trap on the difficulty: the plan's own record carries a premium balance of 45.04, and an agent who
reads that field as the premium still to be collected presents 18.02
rather than 81.06, because the balance is the sum of what has been raised less what has been
paid, while the premium still to be collected is the premium frozen on the plan less what has been
matched. An agent who does not find the factor documents at all books 11.26, 35.00
and 13.77 instead of 81.06, 13.77 and 49.20.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
Write 1 — subject insure_fee_charge. The only base policy whose subject intersects it is
insure_lapse_and_reinstatement, whose gate plan_fee_state reads "A plan fee is raised only while the
plan record stands in the quoted, active, claim_open, claim_settled, lapsed or cancelled state." At
frozen_time the plan stands active (system record, pre-action), so it holds, and the gate's
correlation key insure_holdings.protection_plan_id binds to the call's protection_plan_id.
Write 2 — subject insure_premium_charge. The only base policy whose subject intersects it is
insure_premium_terms, whose gate premium_chargeable_state reads "A premium is raised only while the
plan record stands in the quoted, active, claim_open or claim_settled state." The plan stands active
at that step too — the household's own ending of the plan is the last write of the task, so the state
is not yet cancelled — and the same correlation key binds.
Write 3 — subject insure_cancel. The only base policy whose subject intersects it is
insure_cancellation. Its single gate, within_free_look, is retired by a declared overwrite: this
policy's rule states the whole settlement, the free look branch included, in its own words ("Where
the plan is given up no later than its free look period counted in calendar days from the day the
plan was taken, the anchor day counting as day zero, the whole of the premium collected on the plan
answers for what stands unpaid instead of any unearned part of it"), and that sentence is quoted as
replaced_by against the base sentence it supersedes. Nothing of the free look is lost: it is carried
in the rule and implemented in compute by the days_since_taken binding, which in this world reads 132
days against the tier's free look period of 14, so the free look branch does not apply. The policy
therefore enters solvability_contract at policy_scope, and no time gate governs any of the three
writes, so temporal_feasibility is empty.
Inherited boundaries honoured throughout: the plan is written over one holding of a covered product
line; cover ends on the day the giving up is recorded and not on a day the household nominates (the
tool stamps the day from the frozen clock); and the premium already paid is not returned as money
here — it answers for what stands unpaid, which is exactly what the closing balance records.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The narrowest object is protection plan 5b05f5fb-d7b6-49cc-9a9c-03335c296949 for season 2026-27, written
over pass 1892fab2-8c18-4987-9ea6-314812b249a9. Every aggregate is correlated by that plan id (the premium entries raised, the
payments matched to them, the charges standing, the papers filed, the payouts standing) or by that
pass id (the instalments charged on its schedule, the instalment its payment method refused, its
tier's instalment count and its state). The household's second pass 132dedcf-89f6-4a8d-a4e7-ecfeaff6e3f9 (Imogen's Local Pass,
paid in full) is the deliberate exclusion: it carries its own plan opening and a scan, and neither
may enter the covered holding's counts — every cross-category read in all three policies is filtered
to the covered pass. The charge raised for giving the plan up is tied to the plan alone and carries
the cancellation charge category, which is what separates it from the premium entries on the same
account.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
Root problem: insure_ext_giveup_settlement (tool confirm_plan_giveup_9d16ef5f, owner user — the
household's own write, handed over by the agent). Prerequisite problems: insure_ext_giveup_charge
(tool raise_plan_giveup_charge_59dbe3e5, owner agent) and insure_ext_premium_presentation (tool
present_plan_premium_8deb00b0, owner agent). Two edges, both kind value_input, both form state.
Edge 1, gate premium_raised: "What the plan's premium account is left standing at is worked out only
after every instalment of premium that has fallen due on the plan stands raised on the protection
account." Four-point test: the connective is "only after"; the waited-on side is a record-visible
state (a premium entry standing on the protection account for every presentation that has fallen
due); it names no tool, no policy id and no code token; and its strength is exactly the edge's, a
hard "only after" over the premium entries of this plan alone. Exactly one write in this difficulty
raises premium on a plan — present_plan_premium_8deb00b0, named by
insure_ext_premium_presentation — so the reader can resolve the hop. Unresolved at frozen_time: the
covered pass account carries five instalment charges for the season (94c14f92-257d-4b0e-a021-ea16a1bcea24 through
d9b637ce-81f1-444d-a0ce-8dcb05df0b8b) while the protection account carries only three premium entries (c4028461-b867-4200-a61a-d82eb3854269,
5a8fc9dc-e543-4f06-b8ac-5b8193b1e00b, 6ac11678-e4a1-4092-9f47-28e5513f7731), so two presentations that have fallen due stand unraised. It flips true
when the presentation books 81.06 of premium on the account.
Edge 2, gate fees_standing: "What the plan's premium account is left standing at is settled only once
the charge the plan owes for being given up stands raised on the protection account." Same four-point
test with the connective "only once", waiting on a record-visible state (a charge of that kind
standing on the protection account), and exactly one write in this difficulty raises it —
raise_plan_giveup_charge_59dbe3e5, named by insure_ext_giveup_charge. Unresolved at frozen_time: the
protection account carries premium entries and one payment and nothing else, so no charge of that
kind stands on it. It flips true when the charge of 13.77 is booked.
Derivation for both: the sentence states what the closing figure waits on; the protection account
read back shows the state absent; the depended-on policy's own rule says what its write books (one
premium entry for each presentation that has fallen due; the charge a plan owes for being given up),
and each is the only write that books it. Topological order: the charge, the presentation, then the
household's own ending of the plan. Deletion sensitivity from the Step 5 run: skipping the
presentation leaves the settlement at 0.00 instead of 49.20; skipping the charge
leaves it at 35.43.
ORDER UNIQUENESS. The two prerequisites are parallel and may be resolved in either order. Proof that
both orders leave the same terminal state and the same scored values: the charge policy reads the
plan record, the covered holding's record and the protection account's premium entries and papers,
and books a fee entry; the presentation policy reads the plan record, the covered holding's record
and account and the protection account's premium entries and payments, and books a premium entry.
Neither reads what the other writes — the presentation never reads fee entries, and the charge's only
ledger reads are the latest premium entry date and the count of payments matched to premium entries,
neither of which the presentation writes. The charge's term
anchor tier does not turn on that date in this world (the plan carries a day cover began and is
collected alongside the covered holding's instalments, so the first tier applies), so its figure is
13.77 whichever order is taken, and the presentation's figure is 81.06 whichever
order is taken. Both entries are created with content-hashed ids from their own arguments, so the
terminal rows are identical either way, and the root's own reads take both in as sums.
The customer never mentions either prerequisite: user_scenario says nothing about a charge, a fee, an
instalment, a premium presentation or anything standing unpaid; it asks only for the plan to be
ended. The tool layer blocks nothing: raise_plan_giveup_charge_59dbe3e5 and
present_plan_premium_8deb00b0 each read the plan row only to copy the household reference and the
season onto the entry and then call ctx.create; confirm_plan_giveup_9d16ef5f is a single ctx.update.
None of them looks at whether the other has run, and each writes faithfully and returns its ordinary
receipt whatever the account happens to carry.

FACTOR CARD — insure_ext_giveup_charge (four factors, two parameter and two method).
1. fee_scale (parameter). Tiers: given up no later than the plan's free look period counted from the
   day it was taken -> nothing; more than half the term run -> half the plan's cancellation fee;
   otherwise the whole of it. This world: 132 days since the plan was taken against a free look of
   14, and 89 of the term's 149 days run, so half. Baseline (the whole fee): 26.25.
2. term_anchor (method, cross-difficulty passes). Tiers: the plan's record carries a day cover began
   and the premium is collected alongside the covered holding's instalments -> counted from the day
   cover began; the covered holding's record shows it given up in the season -> from the day it was
   given up; otherwise -> from the day the last premium entry was raised. This world: cover began
   2026-11-20 and Season Pass Protection Premier is collected with the holding's instalments, so
   2026-11-20. Baseline (the day the last premium entry was raised, 2026-12-10) leaves only 69 of 149
   days run, which puts the scale on its fall-through: 26.25.
3. minimum_earned (parameter). Tiers: priced on the value covered and cover run past the waiting
   period -> the minimum earned share of the premium frozen on the plan; priced on the value covered
   and still inside the waiting period -> half that share; otherwise nothing. This world: the tier is
   priced on the value covered and the waiting period ended 2026-11-27, 82 days ago, so 22.52 against
   the scaled fee of 17.50 — the least the collective keeps is what binds. Baseline (nothing kept):
   8.75.
4. charge_relief (parameter, cross-difficulty passes, multi-source). Tiers: the covered holding given
   up in the season -> the whole of the plan's cancellation fee allowed against the charge; the
   protection account carrying a payment matched to a premium entry and the covered holding standing
   active -> the relief share of that fee; otherwise nothing. This world: the payment cebc8a30-0082-4390-b4dd-77d44fac53fb of
   2026-10-10 stands matched to the first premium entry and pass 1892fab2-8c18-4987-9ea6-314812b249a9 stands active, so 8.75 is
   allowed. Baseline (nothing allowed): 22.52.
   Whole-baseline reading: 35.00 against gold 13.77.

FACTOR CARD — insure_ext_premium_presentation (four factors, three parameter and one method).
1. collectible_basis (parameter, multi-source). Tiers: the premium frozen on the plan standing above
   the payments matched to premium entries and the plan's own balance standing below the difference
   -> the premium frozen on the plan less those payments; no payment matched at all -> the whole
   premium frozen on the plan; otherwise the balance the plan's record carries. This world: 225.17
   frozen against 22.52 matched, and a record balance of 45.04 below the difference of 202.65, so
   202.65. Baseline (the record balance): 18.02 — this is the cache trap.
2. schedule_remaining (parameter, cross-difficulty passes, multi-source). Tiers: the covered holding's
   account showing instalments charged in the season and the holding active -> the count its tier
   holds less those charged; no instalment charged and the holding active -> the whole count its tier
   holds; otherwise one. This world: the Collective Elite tier holds ten and five stand charged, so
   five. Baseline (one): 405.30.
3. instalment_measure (method). Tiers: the premium collected alongside the covered holding's
   instalments and instalments still falling -> the amount still to be collected over the instalments
   still to fall; collected in a single payment -> the whole amount still to be collected; otherwise
   over the whole months of the term. This world: the first tier, 202.65 over five, 40.53. Baseline
   (over the term's four whole months): 101.32.
4. presentations_due (parameter, cross-difficulty passes). Tiers: the covered holding's account
   showing more instalments charged than the protection account shows premium entries raised -> one
   for each of the difference; fewer -> none; otherwise one. This world: five charged against three
   raised, so two. Baseline (one): 40.53.
   Whole-baseline reading: 11.26 against gold 81.06.

FACTOR CARD — insure_ext_giveup_settlement (five factors, two parameter and three method).
1. return_basis (parameter). Tiers: the premium frozen on the plan standing above the payments
   matched and the premium collected alongside the covered holding's instalments -> the premium
   frozen on the plan; no payment matched -> nothing; otherwise the total of the payments matched.
   This world: 225.17 against 22.52 matched on a plan collected with the holding's instalments, so
   225.17. Baseline (the payments matched): 130.80.
2. giveup_anchor (method, multi-source). Tiers: no claim made in the season, no paper filed against
   one and no day of closure on the record -> the day the household gives it up; a day of closure on
   the record -> that day; otherwise the day cover began. This world: the plan's record carries no
   claim date and no closure date and no paper has ever been filed, so 2027-02-17. Baseline (the day
   cover began): 0.00.
3. unearned_measure (method, cross-difficulty passes, multi-source). Tiers: premium collected
   alongside the covered holding's instalments and instalments still falling -> the days still to come
   over the days of the term; collected in a single payment -> the whole months still to come over the
   whole months of the term; otherwise the instalments still to fall as a share of all the schedule
   holds. This world: the first tier, 60 days of 149. Baseline (five instalments of ten, a half):
   27.29.
4. return_allowance (parameter, multi-source). Tiers: the plan returning premium pro rata, no payout
   standing this season and the plan given up after the first half of its term has run -> the whole
   of the unearned premium; the same with the plan given up inside the first half of its term -> the
   short-rate share the rule sets, nine tenths of it; otherwise nothing, which is where a plan on
   which a payout stands falls, the cover having already answered for itself. This world: Premier
   returns pro rata, no payout stands and 89 of the term's 149 days have run, so the whole. Baseline
   (nothing returned): 139.87.
5. offset_reach (method, cross-difficulty passes). Tiers: the covered holding's account carrying an
   instalment the payment method refused in the season -> everything standing unpaid is set against
   the unearned premium; no refusal and the covered holding itself given up in the season -> nothing
   at all, what stands unpaid being dealt with on that holding's own settlement; otherwise the
   charges standing unpaid, which is the standard method. This world: the refusal of 2027-01-10 on
   pass 1892fab2-8c18-4987-9ea6-314812b249a9 stands, so all 139.87. Baseline (the charges standing unpaid):
   0.00.
   Whole-baseline reading: 13.77 against gold 49.20.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS.
customers f279c18e-97bf-47ba-840f-4374b4b93212: the household; the mobile number is the locator and the date of birth and
passholder number are the two credentials. Its stored_payment_method is none, which is why a
presentation had to be made by hand rather than taken automatically. passes_holdings 1892fab2-8c18-4987-9ea6-314812b249a9: the
covered holding — its tier fixes the ten instalments the schedule holds, its active state is read by
three separate ladders, and its account is where the refusal stands. passes_holdings 132dedcf-89f6-4a8d-a4e7-ecfeaff6e3f9: the
household's second pass — the near-miss for every covered-holding count, since its own plan opening
and scan sit on the same household account and none of them may be counted. passes_ledger: the plan
opening of each pass, five instalment charges on the covered pass (94c14f92-257d-4b0e-a021-ea16a1bcea24 .. d9b637ce-81f1-444d-a0ce-8dcb05df0b8b),
the refusal d76d6ebd-9b61-49b5-b3e5-a08b657e1b58 of 2027-01-10 with the late fee 777689a9-8a3b-45f2-a142-78e1b87ddab0 that answers it, and six
scans. Remove the refusal and the settlement sets nothing but the charges against the unearned
premium; remove an instalment charge and both the presentation count and the instalments still to
fall move. insure_ledger: three premium entries (c4028461-b867-4200-a61a-d82eb3854269, 5a8fc9dc-e543-4f06-b8ac-5b8193b1e00b, 6ac11678-e4a1-4092-9f47-28e5513f7731), the one
payment cebc8a30-0082-4390-b4dd-77d44fac53fb that matched the first, and the cover of 2649.00 loaded when cover began. Remove
the payment and the collectible basis falls to its second tier; remove a premium entry and the
presentation count moves.
There is no stale cache here and no schema invariant is broken:
insure_holdings.premium_balance_usd is exactly 67.56 raised less 22.52 paid = 45.04, and
benefit_remaining_usd is exactly the 2649.00 loaded with no payout against it;
passes_holdings.installment_balance_usd is 2649.00 committed plus the 35.00 late fee less the four
instalments that cleared, 1624.40. The difficulty is not a broken cache but a reading one: the
balance field answers a different question from the one the presentation asks.

AUTOMATIC-CLAUSE CHECK. Lapse for non-payment does not fire: the tier's grace period is 21 calendar
days and no premium instalment of this plan has been presented and refused — the premium entries
standing unmatched were never presented to an instrument at all, the account carrying none. Expiry is
2027-04-18, after frozen_time. Closure needs nothing left to collect and no allowed claim to pay, and
the plan still carries a balance. On the passes side the refusal of 2027-01-10 is already answered by
the late fee of 2027-01-15, and the Collective Elite tier's suspension threshold is more than one
refusal, so no suspension is owed.

PERSONA DESIGN. Desmond is brisk and unsentimental, the opposite of task 0's tired caller: he states
his decision once, gives the mobile number, holds the date of birth and passholder number until
asked, and declines to quote figures he is not sure of. He volunteers a reason only if asked and it
is a plain change of mind, which is a peril the plans exclude, so nothing in the world tempts a claim
instead. He names nothing of the two prerequisites — no charge, no fee, no instalment, nothing
standing unpaid — and his only contribution to them is the passive line that fires once the agent
explains the ending has to be recorded by him and hands it across. His stopping condition is the
agent telling him the plan is ended and what the account is left standing at, which answers the last
gold action exactly and asks for nothing beyond it.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. He gives the mobile number; the agent finds the household and
verifies with two stated details; the plans, the passes, the protection account and the household's
pass accounts are read; the agent raises the charge for giving the plan up and presents the premium
that has fallen due, then unlocks the ending of the plan and hands it to him; he records it, and the
receipt enters the shared transcript; the agent tells him what the account is left standing at. Every
call is synchronous under one frozen_time. Nothing waits on a payment clearing, a review or a future
date: the closing balance is a figure on the record, and the household settles it afterwards in its
own time, which is not a step of this task.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Read the household, verify, read the plan, both passes, the protection account and
the household's pass account entries. The settlement rule waits on two states, and the records show
neither: no charge of that kind stands on the protection account, and the covered pass's schedule has
been charged five times against three premium entries on the plan. Raise the charge first: the free
look of 14 days ran out long ago and 89 of the term's 149 days have run from the day cover began, so
the charge stands at half the plan's cancellation fee, 17.50; the plan is priced on the value covered
and the waiting period ended 82 days ago, and the plan is long out of its free look period, so the
least the collective keeps is a tenth of the 225.17 premium, 22.52, and the greater of the two is
taken; a payment stands matched to the first premium entry and the covered pass stands active, so a
quarter of the plan's cancellation fee, 8.75, is allowed against it, giving
13.77. Then present the premium: the premium still to be collected is 225.17 less the 22.52
matched, 202.65, not the 45.04 the plan's balance shows; five instalments still fall on the covered
pass's schedule of ten, so one instalment is 40.53; five charges against three premium entries means
two presentations have fallen due, giving 81.06. Then hand the ending of the plan to the
household: the account then stands unpaid at 148.62 raised plus 13.77 in charges less 22.52
matched, 139.87; the unearned premium is worked out on the 225.17 frozen on the plan, for the 60 days
of 149 still to come from today, at the whole share Premier returns, 90.67; the refusal on the covered
pass account means everything unpaid is set against it, leaving 49.20 standing.

VERIFICATION RUN. The handling-time recomputation was executed with the gate's own evaluator over
this initial_state, each computation on the world its own step stands in:
insure_ext_giveup_charge -> 13.77; insure_ext_premium_presentation -> 81.06;
insure_ext_giveup_settlement -> 49.20. Factor sensitivity, one baseline substituted at a time:
fee_scale 26.25, term_anchor 26.25, minimum_earned
8.75, charge_relief 22.52; collectible_basis
18.02, schedule_remaining 405.30,
instalment_measure 101.32, presentations_due
40.53; return_basis 130.80, giveup_anchor
0.00, unearned_measure 27.29,
return_allowance 139.87, offset_reach 0.00. Whole
baselines: 35.00, 11.26, 13.77. Prerequisite sensitivity: skipping the
presentation gives 0.00, skipping the charge gives 35.43, both against
49.20. Every figure differs from its gold, so no factor and no edge is decorative.

TWO-WAY EQUIVALENCE (rule <-> compute). Forward: every binding that reads the world or makes a choice
carries a verbatim quotation in compute_basis — the ledger aggregates (premium_raised,
premium_matched, fees_standing, premium_raised_count, claim_papers, claim_papers_filed,
payouts_standing, last_premium_date), the cross-category reads (holding_state, holding_closed_date,
holding_standing, schedule_instalments, schedule_instalments_held, holding_charged,
schedule_instalments_charged, refused_instalments_held), every ladder binding, and the ordering,
bounds and rounding bindings (result in all three policies, account_unpaid, unearned_premium).
Reverse sweep: every load-bearing sentence is claimed — the "greater of the two ... before anything
is allowed against it" sentence by the charge's result, the "each instalment having been rounded to
the cent before that multiplication" sentence by the presentation's result, the "worked out first and
in full, and only then set against what is unpaid" sentence by the settlement's result, the free look
sentence by days_since_taken and unearned_premium, and the two prerequisite sentences by
premium_raised and fees_standing. The acting base and the moment of each operation are pinned in
prose: the allowance is taken off the greater of the two amounts and never off the cancellation fee
before the comparison; the share the plan returns acts on the amount the return is worked out on
after the part of the term still to come has been taken of it, and never on what stands unpaid.
Rounding is stated per instalment in the presentation and at the end elsewhere, and the interval
conventions are stated: calendar days from the day the plan was taken with the anchor day as day
zero for the free look, days from the day treated as given up to the day cover is due to end over the
days from the day cover began to that same day for the unearned part.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this
worklog masked, and only the prose to be published, the tool schemas, the finder returns and the
persona in view: the settlement document states two waits, and the protection account read back shows
neither state; the charge document is the only one describing what a plan owes for being given up and
the presentation document the only one describing premium raised on a plan, so the two hops resolve
uniquely, and the ending itself is the household's own tool. The figures then follow from the
thirteen factor documents, every one of which is findable from the finder returns (the plan's dates
and premium, the payments matched, the covered pass's tier and state, its five instalment charges and
its refusal, the absence of papers and payouts). The order of the two prerequisites is free and
provably immaterial. Both the order and all three figures come out as gold, and no second reading
survives: the premium still to be collected is fixed against the premium frozen on the plan rather
than the balance field, and the day the plan is treated as given up from is fixed by the record
carrying no closure date.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD. gold_actions[7] (the charge) is on_request, its intent the
caller's own words cited verbatim, its discriminator the phrase "give up the protection plan on my
pass", its base precondition insure_lapse_and_reinstatement.plan_fee_state evidenced by the plan
row's protection_plan_id and status with the correlation key bound to the call's protection_plan_id.
gold_actions[9] (the presentation) is state_due, so its intent is the system's own record — the
premium entries standing on the account against the instalments charged on the covered pass — and its
base precondition is insure_premium_terms.premium_chargeable_state on the same key. gold_actions[11]
(the household's own ending of the plan) is on_request on the same cited phrase, with
insure_cancellation at policy_scope because its only gate is retired by this policy's declared
overwrite. temporal_feasibility is empty. seed_consistency covers the plan row and all five
protection account entries.


REVISION 2 — items closed from the source-layer policy-task audit (round 1 report:
env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/audits/policy_task/pass_protection_desk/). Symptom -> root cause -> change ->
re-run result. Both prerequisite problems and the root keep their scored values, so this task's tree,
edges, factor weights and unique solution are unchanged: 13.77, 81.06 and
49.20 as before.

F-RED-1 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, charter-global; bears on this task's charge problem). Symptom: a plan
given up inside its free look period was charged the least amount the collective keeps — 22.52 on the
audit's own worked case — while base insure_cancellation says the premium comes back in full inside
that period and the only charge base names, the cancellation fee, is already declared superseded.

user_scenario:
You are Desmond Achterberg, fifty-seven, a structural engineer in Provo who has
had a pass at Silverpine Basin for most of two decades and buys one for his wife Imogen as well. You
are calling the guest services centre in the middle of a Wednesday morning between site visits, brisk
and unbothered, because the household has been going through the standing costs and the protection
you took on your own pass in October is one of the things you have decided to stop. Nothing has gone
wrong and nobody is hurt; you have simply decided you would rather not carry it for the rest of the
season, and if the agent asks why you say exactly that, that you have changed your mind about wanting
it and would not take it again. What you say you want is to give up the protection plan on my pass,
today rather than at the end of the month, and you would like to know where that leaves you when it
is done. You are content for the agent to do their side of it without checking each step with you,
and you will do in person anything that only you can do, provided they say so while you are on the
line.

You give the mobile number as 3035550561 when you are asked how the household is found. If more is
needed you give your date of birth as 1969-03-15, or the passholder number off the media, which is
GR45027641, and you can give the postal code 84604 or the email d.achterberg@wasatchpost.com if
either of those is wanted instead. You have no plan reference and say so; you tell the agent it will
be on the account under your name. The pass itself stays as it is, and if you are asked you say yes,
you are still skiing on it. If you are asked whether anyone in the household has made a claim on the
protection this season you say no, never, that is rather the point of stopping it. If the agent asks
what you have paid on the plan so far you say you honestly could not tell them off the top of your
head and would rather they read it off their own records; you do not quote numbers you are not sure
of.

You have no idea how the collective works any of this out and you do not pretend to. If the agent
tells you a figure you take it without haggling. If the agent explains that the ending of the plan
has to be recorded by you rather than by them and hands that across to you, you do it there and then
without fuss; you do not offer to do it until it has been put to you, and if the agent never mentions
it you simply wait and let them work. Once the agent tells you the plan is ended and what your
account is left standing at, you say right, that is understood, you will settle it the usual way, and
you let the call finish there without raising anything else.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record that the caller is the household on screen, comparing the two details he states against the profile on file.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read back the protection plan on the household account with its state, its covered holding, the premium frozen on it, the balance its record carries, the dates cover began, ends and the waiting period ended, and whether any claim stands on it.

Both orders were run and leave the same terminal state and the same scored values: the charge policy reads the plan record, the covered holding's record and the protection account's premium entry dates and papers filed, and books a fee entry; the presentation policy reads the plan record, the covered holding's record and account and the protection account's premium entries and payments, and books a premium entry. Neither reads what the other writes — the presentation never reads fee entries, and the charge's term anchor does not turn on the latest premium entry date in this world because the plan carries a day cover began and is collected alongside the covered holding's instalments, so its first tier applies either way. The charge is 13.77 and the presentation 81.06 whichever order is taken, both entries are created with content-hashed ids from their own arguments, and the settlement reads both as sums, so the terminal rows and the closing figure of 49.20 are identical.
